label: Pharisees test Jesus: is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife?
statement: Pharisees came to Jesus, testing him, and asked whether it is lawful for a man to divorce his wife.
note: Mark asks the question without Matthew's qualifier 'for any cause' (Matthew 19:3).

label: Divorce and remarriage as adultery - no exception clause
statement: 'Whoever divorces his wife, and marries another, commits adultery against her' - Mark states the rule with no exception clause.
note: Matthew 19:9 excepts 'for sexual immorality' and adds a clause about the divorced woman's remarriage; a difference between Gospels, recorded with related_to, never evidence.

label: A woman who divorces her husband
statement: 'If a woman herself divorces her husband, and marries another, she commits adultery' - Mark's wording presumes a woman could divorce her husband, a case Matthew does not address.
note: Josephus says Salome's divorce of Costobarus was 'not according to the Jewish laws' (complicates edge), and the fetched Wikipedia 'Women in Judaism' states that in biblical times a wife could not divorce a husband without his consent; the tension is recorded, not smoothed away.

label: 'Do not defraud' in the commandment list
statement: Mark's list of commandments includes 'Do not defraud' (me apostereseis), which Matthew's list does not have.

label: 'Taking up the cross' in the call to the rich man
statement: Jesus tells the man to come and follow him, 'taking up the cross' - a detail Matthew omits in the parallel (Matthew 19:21).

label: James and John ask for the seats at right and left
statement: James and John, the sons of Zebedee, asked Jesus to grant them to sit, one at his right hand and one at his left hand, in his glory.

label: Great = your servant; first = bondservant of all
statement: 'Whoever wants to become great among you shall be your servant, and whoever of you wants to become first among you shall be bondservant of all.'

label: Bartimaeus son of Timaeus cries out at Jericho
statement: At Jericho, Bartimaeus son of Timaeus, a blind beggar, sat by the road and cried out, 'Jesus, you son of David, have mercy on me.'

label: Bartimaeus receives his sight
statement: Bartimaeus asked, 'Rabboni, that I may see again'; Jesus said, 'Go your way. Your faith has made you well', and immediately he received his sight and followed him on the way.
note: A healing; searched honestly and found no external evidence - the setting evidence is attached to claim:mk-10-46-47-bartimaeus and claim:mt-20-29-out-of-jericho.
